editorial.headline: Taxi Transport: Nationally Open, With a Clear Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers metered, door-to-door taxi passenger transport within a limited operating area, open nationally to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Taxi transport, in this classification, is a tightly defined passenger-service activity rather than a catch-all for moving people by car. It covers journeys in specially marked passenger vehicles fitted with taximeters, serving passengers door to door within a limited operating area. The definition matters because it places the commercial centre of gravity on a recognisable taxi operation: a marked vehicle, a metered fare mechanism, and a bounded territory of operation.

The activity is open across the full stated range of business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That makes it relevant to operators entering at a modest scale as well as to larger businesses building a more substantial transport presence. The record does not divide the activity into separate commercial models within those scales; its common thread is the same taxi service described above. A registration should therefore be read through that practical service: passenger transport by specially marked, taximeter-equipped cars, offered from door to door in a limited area.

Nationally, the position is direct. The PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain terms, foreign investment is fully open at the national level for this activity. The stated basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-ownership ceiling in the record to qualify that national position, so the ownership reading is not a partial-opening story: it is a fully open one.

Bali requires a separate reading, but it is not a contradiction. The provincial moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island on a permanent basis. This activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK because, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi; the record expressly says it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. For a foreign investor, that is the honest conclusion: taxi transport is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali does not block PMA registration for this activity under the stated moratorium. The Bali position rests on the recorded higher-risk treatment at the Besar scale, not on an invented exemption or a separate ownership cap.
